clue.text: Courageous animals hunted for sport

blocks.note: first meaning: plucky, willing to have a go
second meaning: wild creatures pursued by hunters and shooters

explanation.surface: Brave beasts being chased down by hunters.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one description of bold quarry; it is really two separate senses of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning plucky and ready for anything, and also a noun for wild birds and beasts shot or hunted.

clue.text: One who likes to eat a portion of anything our man doesn’t

indicators.note: a portion of means only a slice of the following words is used, running across them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the last

explanation.surface: A food lover eats a share of whatever our fellow leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across anythinG OUR MAN Doesn't.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand is a person who enjoys eating heartily, sometimes to excess, a lover of good food.

clue.text: Make fun of practice examination

blocks.note: first meaning: ridicule or tease
second meaning: a trial exam sat before the real one

explanation.surface: Laugh at a trial run of a test.
explanation.walkthrough: A mock is the British school name for a rehearsal exam taken before the real public exam.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to ridicule; as a noun, British schools use it for a rehearsal test.

clue.text: Role model is generous, putting former partner first

indicators.note: the instruction tells us to place the former partner at the front, before the word for generous

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
ample means plentiful, generous in quantity

explanation.surface: Someone admired as a role model is praised for being generous after an ex comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is someone whose behaviour others copy, a person who sets a good pattern to follow.

clue.text: Person fleeing from corrupt regime

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or twisted out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the six letters of regime

explanation.surface: Someone escaping a crooked government.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is exactly the story of a political exile, so the answer belongs in the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigre is someone who has left their home country, usually for political reasons, an exile.

clue.text: Satiric actor cast as nobleman

definitions.note: adjective: in the manner of a nobleman

indicators.note: cast means thrown or moulded into a new form, so the letters take a new shape

blocks.note: all twelve letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A satirical performer is given the role of a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: Cast looks like theatre casting, fitting the actor; it is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocratic describes the bearing or rank of a member of the titled upper class, as a lord would be.

clue.text: Precisely identify purpose of personal identification number?

blocks.note: PIN is the abbreviation for this bank-card code
the point of something is its purpose

explanation.surface: Pin down exactly what a bank-card number is for.
explanation.walkthrough: Purpose of X reads as X's point, so the code comes first and the purpose follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinpoint is to locate or name something with great accuracy, finding its exact position.

clue.text: What may be used by anglers to release river fish

indicators.note: to release means to let go, so the river letter is dropped from the anglers' equipment

blocks.clueFragment: What may be used by anglers
blocks.note: anglers wind in line on reels
R is the usual abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Something fishermen use to let go of fish they caught in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from REELS leaves EELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snake-like fish found in rivers and the sea, a specific example of fish.

clue.text: Popular period at home with expert is boring

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
a term is a period, such as a school term
to be in is to be at home
able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: A trendy spell at home with a specialist is dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Interminable means seemingly endless, tediously long, so dull and tiresome to sit through.

clue.text: Like offer of university place with no qualifications?

definitions.text: Like offer of university place with no qualifications?

blocks.clueFragment: Like offer of university place with no qualifications?
blocks.note: surface reading: a place offered to a student who has no exam results at all
setter's reading: qualifications are conditions or provisos, so an offer with none attached is a firm one with no strings

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, universities make offers either dependent on exam grades or with no grade requirement at all; the question mark flags the pun on qualifications.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means absolute, without any conditions, provisos or reservations attached, as in a firm admission offer.

clue.text: English king and queen fall from grace

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
R for rex, Latin for king
R for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An English royal couple suffers a public disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: King and queen both give R, from the Latin rex and regina used in royal monograms.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to sin or make a moral mistake, which is what falling from grace means.

clue.text: Detest violent crime against men

indicators.note: against means placed right next to, so the two parts sit side by side

blocks.note: ABH is actual bodily harm, an assault offence in English law
OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Someone hates acts of violence committed against men.
explanation.walkthrough: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a British criminal charge; 'men' as OR, other ranks, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to loathe or regard it with disgust, a strong synonym for hate.

clue.text: Distressed asset mostly hidden by firm

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
hidden by means concealed inside, so the shortened word goes within the word for firm

blocks.note: hard means firm, solid
asset taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A troubled asset is mostly concealed by a company.
explanation.walkthrough: Firm looks like a company in the surface, but here it is an adjective meaning solid or rigid.
explanation.definitionFit: Harassed means worried and strained by pressure, the state of being troubled and stressed.

clue.text: Great book about author’s generating strong feelings

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so the word for a great book is read backwards

blocks.note: a tome is a large heavy volume
the author says 'I have', contracted to I'VE

explanation.surface: A weighty novel about its writer stirs up powerful emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the author is the setter, who refers to themself as I; so author's is I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emotive arouses intense passion or feeling, such as a contentious subject or a moving speech.

clue.text: Part of Somerset he realised is heavenly

indicators.note: part of means only a slice of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters span the end of the county name, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that a corner of Somerset is divine.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across somersET HE REALised; Somerset is a rural English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicate and otherworldly, as if from the sky or heaven above, celestial.

clue.text: Spiritual figure beginning to dither and shiver uncontrollably

indicators.note: beginning to points at only the opening letter of the following word
uncontrollably suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: the first letter of dither
the six letters of shiver, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A holy man starts to waver and shake without control.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits a whirling dervish nicely, since dervishes spin in ecstatic dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A dervish is a member of a Sufi Muslim order known for ascetic devotion, a religious figure.

clue.text: Enthusiastic male interested in culture

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
someone arty is keen on the arts

explanation.surface: A keen man who loves the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty means warm, vigorous and wholehearted, full of lively zeal and cheer.

clue.text: Unpleasant individual recounted gag

indicators.note: recounted means told out loud, so we want a word that is spoken like the one for an unpleasant individual

blocks.note: a wretch is a nasty or despicable person; the silent W leaves the sound unchanged

explanation.surface: A nasty person retold a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: Gag looks like a joke being told, but here it is the verb for heaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to choke or heave as if about to vomit, the same physical reflex as to retch.

clue.text: Revolutionary lives for some time

indicators.note: a revolution is a turning round, so the word for lives is turned backwards

blocks.note: they are means they exist or live

explanation.surface: A revolutionary lives for a while somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a lengthy period of history, a span marked by particular events or character.

clue.text: Argument leads to tears in full flow

indicators.note: leads are the front runners, so only the opening letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A quarrel ends with someone crying uncontrollably.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a row that ends in floods of tears, which suits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel or minor squabble, typically between friends or partners.

clue.text: Worthless support

blocks.note: first meaning: low, without moral value
second meaning: the foundation something stands on

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means low or ignoble; as a noun it is the bottom part that holds something up.

clue.text: Debar unionist actively refusing to submit to authority

indicators.note: actively suggests the letters are busy and moving about, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: all thirteen letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Bar a trade unionist who is busily defying the bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a militant union member being banned, which suits the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Insubordinate describes defiance of superiors, disobedient behaviour toward people in charge.

clue.text: Developing edgy fit?

indicators.note: developing means changing or forming into something new, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the seven letters of these two words

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue serves as definition too: someone coming down with a nervous fit would be restless and twitchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fidgety means restless and unable to keep still, the physical sign of jittery nerves.

clue.text: Healthy source of water

blocks.note: first meaning: in good health, not ill
second meaning: a shaft sunk into the ground to draw water

explanation.surface: A spring that supplies wholesome water.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means fit and not sick; the noun is a dug shaft from which water is drawn up.
